column1: # replay fixes 2026-11-18: complete corrected rows for _rules_index.tsv, replace by file name; columns: file, status, seats, family, triggers, enforced_by, rule

column7: In a brief, for every 'verify X from Y': open Y, confirm it answers X today; a file the agent must repair is never ground truth. Queued tickets carry scope and seat authority. Read the mail against ITSELF (a hold stated elsewhere); a change says SUPERSEDES.

When I read or quote a capped, sorted or filtered list: state ORDER, bound and PREDICATE with the count (allow-lists); count items myself; when two counts disagree get the breakdown first; 'quiet since X' needs a window from the other party's last write.

Never chain a destructive step (kill, pane close, launch, deploy, delete) after a step that can refuse or a guard read (pgrep, uptime), in one command or pipe: read rc and output, then act. Gate verifiers on the action's success; assert the subject exists.

When writing any line that reports a send, tap, card, ack or launch (panel, note, mail, provenance): write it in a LATER call, from the tool's output ('launched %11, verified HH:MM'); before that say what I am doing. If a refusal would falsify it, hold it.

In another project's checkout: git read verbs only (diff, show, log, rev-list, ls-remote, cat-file); for status use git --no-optional-locks status (plain status writes .git/index). A hook refuses fetch, merge-tree --write-tree, worktree, checkout, commit.

When running parallel seats on one project (Kam's grant): partition by directory, breach STOP in both briefs, own worktree each, atomic mkdir push lock (never pgrep), seat numbers from project history, kills by ancestry, shared-inbox warning in every brief.

Before writing 'ratified', 'endorsed' or 'required leg' to an agent: open the artefact; a required leg must REACH the change; else say 'received, goes to the gate, unread by me'. Ratify shapes; product claims go to the gate; retract dead requirements by name.

At each checkpoint, before any handover or wrap, and with every card add or panel message: run kam_rulings_today.sh and reconcile_rulings.py (report, then --apply for this seat's scope) before writing what Kam has ruled. Check the ACTION behind a late tap.

Before asking Kam a question or sending a claim: verify each load-bearing premise at source; mark agent prose 'reported, unverified'. Measure the WHOLE space before any negative claim, and quote the written rule before saying X needs Kam.

Before a hand-rolled fleet action: ls fleet/, fleet/cockpit/, tools/ for the tool; read its header before first use (what a bare call does). Taps go via cockpit.sh say --mail, never raw tmux send-keys; Kam's messages via kam_msgs.sh; a refusal is the answer.
